# Title

Testing the wind disruption hypothesis for beetle refugia

Stand density, terrain and wind as competing controls on mountain pine beetle attack (Dendroctonus ponderosae) in the Selkirk Mountains of British Columbia

# Running title

Wind disruption and beetle refugia

<!-- 34 characters including spaces, against the 40-character limit. -->

# Keywords

Dendroctonus ponderosae, forest disturbance, insect outbreaks, Landsat time series,

# Acknowledgements

This work received no external funding. Beetle disturbance was classified from Landsat
Collection 2 Level-2 surface reflectance distributed by the United States Geological
Survey; stand structure came from the British Columbia Data Catalogue; terrain from
Natural Resources Canada; and wind from Environment and Climate Change Canada. The
author thanks those agencies for maintaining the open archives this study rests on.

# Funding statement

This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public,
commercial or not-for-profit sectors.

# Conflict of interest

The author declares no conflict of interest.

# Ethics approval statement

This study used only publicly archived remote sensing, forest inventory and
meteorological data. No animals, human participants or protected material were
involved, so no ethics approval was required.

# Patient consent statement

Not applicable. This study involved no human participants.

# Permission to reproduce

Not applicable. All figures were produced by the author from the public datasets named
in the data availability statement. No material is reproduced from other sources.

# Clinical trial registration

Not applicable.

# Data availability statement

All derived data and the complete analysis code that reproduce every number, table and
figure in this article are archived at Dryad under doi:PLACEHOLDER-DRYAD-DOI, and are
mirrored at <https://github.com/seamusrobertmurphy/beetle-topography-and-wind-study>.
